target_customer: Building system integrators and contractors (fire, HVAC, plumbing, security) that do takeoffs, design and field work
problem: Integrators mark up plans, organize documents and do takeoffs and design by hand. Semble uses AI to speed takeoffs, design and field coordination.
business_model: B2B SaaS for contractors and integrators (pricing not found)
product_category: AI software for building systems design and takeoffs

founders.name: Jonathan Tyshler
founders.background_notes: YC page and long description: met Ethan studying CS at Stanford; worked at Convergint, a large building system integrator.

founders.name: Ethan Boyers
founders.background_notes: No prior employer listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reading construction drawings, extracting devices and quantities and producing design output is applied vision and LLM work with domain specifics, feasible for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Takeoff and plan markup tools are numerous and AI features are being added to them; founder access to integrators through Convergint experience is the main edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Takeoff vendors added AI assist features in 2025 and 2026, but sources found do not tie them to the building systems design wedge.

market_need_then: Takeoff, design and field work in building systems are labor heavy; the company's own pitch is that AI can speed them. No dated demand data was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses sembleai.com; the AI suffix was added to the name.

identity.logo: Not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Short and direct: 'Takeoffs, design, and field work. Powered by AI.'

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand; the site fetched held only a title and tagline, and the name is shared with other firms.

outcome_analysis: Semble is an active Fall 2025 company founded by two Stanford classmates, one of whom worked at the integrator Convergint. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news was found. Funding beyond the YC deal is not confirmed, and no traction data is public. AI takeoff tools from other vendors expanded through 2025 and 2026, so differentiation will depend on the building systems focus.
notes: There are two YC listings, semble and semble-ai, with the same founders and different descriptions (takeoffs and field work versus building system design); they likely describe the same company but this is not confirmed. Funding reports conflict: $500K pre-seed on VCBacked, $1M total with an accelerator tag on Caplight, and an implausible $30M with a Series C on StartupHub; none is primary so no round is recorded. Competitors are empty because the takeoff products found were dated 2026 or were not close to the building systems wedge, so they are not competition as of founding. Completeness pass: the $500K pre-seed of Dec 2025 is recorded from VCBacked and Employbl (databases); EveryDev and Neuronfeed give other stages and dates, and the $30M Series C claim stays unrecorded.
